owner: CC gates writes to cairn/devices/inference_domain/ (its charter's gated_by). No spec question stands at Akien's gate here: whether the meter should account for a refusal at all is settled by the charter's own how_it_learns, not by a ruling.
children: none, because the whole change is one dict key and one tooth at one address (cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py, yield_report at line 302) plus its probe; a decomposition here would be ceremony over a single seam. The larger question it touches — that the verdict vocabulary is enforced by no CHECK constraint because db_domain has no migration primitive — is a SIBLING cast, not a child of this one, and is being cast in the same sitting.

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: the distinct verdict values found past the era, the count of rows at each, the set yield_report accounts for, and the arithmetic difference between calls and the accounted sum (zero is the passing value).
watchme.consumer: whoever next reads the librarian's or the extractor's live output and needs the numbers to add up — and the next builder to add a verdict value, who should find this red rather than discover the under-count in a print months later.
watchme.enough: enough when the store has carried all three accounted verdicts past the era (at least one 'hit', one 'miss' and one 'refused') with the identity calls == hits + misses + refused holding on every read, and no unaccounted verdict value has appeared. The first half proves the accounting is exercised rather than merely written; the second is the standing question, which is why this watch is not a restatement of the build tooth — the tooth reads a corpus the build made, the probe reads the vocabulary the world produces.
watchme.trigger: each read of inference_calls — the probe collects the DISTINCT verdict values actually present in the store past its era and compares them against the set yield_report accounts for. It rides traffic that already exists and needs no clock and no host.
